featureRef: 4.10 Crediting a wrong charge already paid
name: Credit a charge that was wrong but has already been paid, and hold the money against the household
priorityReason: Where a wrong charge has been paid the school is holding money that is not its own, and nothing else in the module puts that right.

goal.capability: to credit a wrong charge the family has already paid and hold the amount against their household
goal.outcome: the family is not out of pocket, the school is not holding money it should not have, and the credit reaches the next bill by itself

secondaryActors.involvement: Approves the credit. Accounts cannot raise and grant it alone.
Sees the credit on the household account and a reduced next challan.

additional.description: A cancellation is attempted on a charge that turns out to have been paid, which routes here instead.
A payment correction leaves money on the household with nothing to apply it to.

preconditions.condition: An issued invoice exists against which money has been received (BR-2).

establishedBy.name: Recording a payment and issuing the receipt

preconditions.condition: The charge itself was wrong — the wrong amount, the wrong student or a charge that should never have been raised.

establishedBy.name: Issuing fee invoices at different scopes

postConditions: The invoice reads Credited, and the amount credited is no longer treated as the school's income.
A credit balance exists against the family code, held as a liability because the money belongs to the family and not to the school.
The credit reaches the next invoice raised for any child in that household automatically, without anybody remembering it.
The original charge and the original payment both stay in place. Nothing has been deleted or edited.
The family has been told they hold a credit and that their next bill will be reduced by it.
No cash has left the school. A credit is not a refund, and money is returned in cash only through the refund use case.
The credit carries its reason, who raised it and who approved it, so money held on a household account can be explained.
The school's income figures have fallen by the credited amount, and its liabilities have risen by the same.

businessRules.rule: A credit is raised by one person and approved by another. Money returned to a household is not something one hand decides alone.
This use case applies only where money has been received. An unpaid wrong charge is cancelled instead, and using a credit for it would create a liability against money the school never took.
The credit is held against the family code, not the individual student. The household is billed as one unit, and a parent expects an overpayment for one child to offset a sibling.
A reason and a written description are mandatory. Money sitting on a household account has to be explainable years later.
The invoice is never edited. Its status moves to Credited and its lines are left exactly as they were.
The amount credited may not exceed what was actually received against the invoice. Crediting more than was paid would hand the family money the school never took from them.
The original payment stays in place and is never reversed. The money did arrive, and pretending otherwise breaks reconciliation against the bank.
The credit sits as a liability until it is used, and is applied automatically to the next invoice raised for any child in that household. It is not returned in cash.
The posting reduces income and raises a liability. It is never an expense, because the school collected the money rather than spending it.
A credit is not a refund. Money leaves the school only through the refund use case, which has its own approval.
A credit may be raised for part of what was paid, where only part of the charge was wrong.
The family is told they hold a credit and that their next bill will be reduced by it, so a smaller challan is expected rather than queried.
A credit cannot be raised against an invoice already cancelled, credited or written off.

basicFlow.userAction: Identifies a charge that was wrong and against which money was collected.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks a payment has been recorded, and refuses where none has, naming the cancellation route instead.

basicFlow.navigation: Student invoice → Credit charge → Raise credit
basicFlow.userAction: Raises a credit, not a write-off, selecting the reason and describing what went wrong.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the amount does not exceed what was received, and sets the credit to Awaiting approval.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the credit and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval with who gave it and when.
Reduces income and raises a liability against the family code. The original charge and the original payment both stay in place.
Holds the amount against the household rather than the individual student, so it can offset any child's bill.
Tells the family they hold a credit and that their next bill will be reduced by it.
Applies the credit automatically to the next invoice raised for any child in that household, drawing the balance down.

alternateFlows.condition: No money was received against the charge
alternateFlows.behaviour: This is a cancellation, not a credit. Raising a credit would create a liability against money the school never took (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: Only part of the charge was wrong
alternateFlows.behaviour: A credit is raised for that part only, and the rest of the payment stands against the correct portion of the charge (BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: The household has several children enrolled
alternateFlows.behaviour: The credit is held against the family code, so it reduces whichever child's invoice is raised next rather than waiting for the child it arose from (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin does not accept the credit
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts with a written reason and nothing is credited in the meantime.

alternateFlows.condition: The family withdraws before the credit is used
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Household account → Request refund
alternateFlows.behaviour: The unused credit is refunded through the refund use case, which has its own approval. A credit alone never returns cash (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A payment correction has left money on the household
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Household account → Raise credit
alternateFlows.behaviour: The money already on the household is recorded as a credit against the family code rather than left unattached.

departures.requirement: Held credit is a liability, never income, and is reported as such until it is applied or refunded.
The original charge and the original payment are never altered. A credit is always an additional entry.
A household credit is drawn down exactly once, even where invoices for two siblings are raised at the same moment.
Credits and their postings are retained 7 years as financial records, and a held credit is retained until it is applied or refunded however long that takes.

openQuestions.question: Does a held credit expire, and what happens to it if a household never uses it?
openQuestions.assumption: No expiry is specified, and unclaimed credit accumulating as a liability needs a policy.

openQuestions.question: Should a family be able to ask for a refund rather than hold a credit, before they withdraw?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The workflow says money is not returned in cash, but a family may insist.

openQuestions.question: Where siblings are in different branches, which branch's account holds the credit?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and family codes may span branches.

openQuestions.question: Is there a value above which the Principal rather than the School Admin should approve a credit?
Should a held credit be shown to the family in the portal, or only on the next challan?
openQuestions.assumption: In the portal, on the household account. Not confirmed.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
